signs.text: MERLIN'S CAVE. The sea has cut a way right through the rock under Tintagel Island. Legend has the infant Arthur washed up here, and Merlin there to find him. The poet Tennyson came to Tintagel in 1848.

text: The walls are slick and black, and the whole cave breathes with the swell, in and out, like something asleep that would rather not be asked.
Through the mouth of the cave a slice of Atlantic is framed in black rock, with a wave in it. It looks like a painting nobody has paid for.
Tennyson came to Tintagel looking for Arthur. This is a good place to be looking.
A mussel shell lies at your feet, polished by the swell. You take one shell, and only one.
